meta.description: Research Series A and cost benchmarks

user.t:
Web research, read-only (no installs, write nothing except your final answer). Date 2026-10-12. Context: scoup.ai, a pre-revenue B2B SaaS / contingency-fee freight-cost recovery startup (Norwegian founder, product built, no customers yet), planning to sell to US mid-size shippers/importers and brokers. We need defensible, cited numbers for a business plan and financial model. Find (URL + grade A/B/C for each; A = primary data like Carta/PitchBook-NVCA reports, BLS, official price pages; B = reputable press/industry benchmark; C = blogs/estimates):
1. Series A benchmarks 2025-2026: median/typical Series A round size and pre/post-money valuation (Carta State of Private Markets, PitchBook-NVCA Venture Monitor, Europe: Atomico State of European Tech / Dealroom), typical dilution, typical ARR/traction at Series A for B2B SaaS (e.g. $1-3M ARR), time from seed to A, and seed benchmarks (since the company may be seed-stage). Note the 2025-26 AI premium if documented.
2. Burn/runway norms: months of runway a Series A should fund (18-30), headcount at A.
3. Cost benchmarks: fully loaded salaries for software engineers, ML engineers, account executives (SaaS, US mid-market quota), sales engineers, customer success, security engineer — US and Norway/Oslo (Norway: SSB or Glassdoor/Levels.fyi; employer social security 14.1% + pension); SOC 2 Type II audit cost; penetration test cost; AWS costs for a small SaaS; cyber insurance and E&O for SaaS; legal (US entity, FMC/regulatory counsel hourly rates).
4. B2B SaaS GTM benchmarks: CAC payback, magic number, sales cycle for mid-market logistics software, net revenue retention benchmarks, gross margin benchmarks (SaaS 75-80%; services-heavy lower), freight audit contingency fee norms (20-50% of recoveries), freight audit pricing per invoice.
5. Logistics-tech VC context 2024-2026: funding totals and notable rounds (e.g. FreightWaves/PitchBook logistics tech reports).
Return a compact cited report (~1300 words) with tables and the 12 most decision-relevant numbers for sizing a Series A and building a 5-year model.

handback.t:
## Funding benchmarks for scoup.ai's Series A sizing and 5-year model (as of 2026-10-12)

The research hit the session's web-search limit (200 calls) partway through. Gaps are listed in section 6. Grades: A = primary source (Carta, PitchBook-NVCA, BLS, SSB, Skatteetaten, vendor price pages); B = reputable press or industry survey; C = blog or estimate. Where a figure from a primary publisher reached me only through a secondary page (because Carta returns 403 to the fetch tool), I graded it B and named the publisher.

### 1. Series A and seed benchmarks

| Metric | Value | Source | Grade |
|---|---|---|---|
| US Series A median pre-money, Q2 2026 | **$62–64M** (two write-ups of the same PitchBook report give different figures). It was $21M in 2020 | PitchBook Q2 2026 via [TheNextWeb](https://thenextweb.com/news/pitchbook-q2-2026-megadeals-87-percent-us-venture-vintage-discount) and [Crowdfund Insider](https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2026/05/278766-us-venture-capital-ecosystem-reaches-9-4t-market-value-report-reveals/) | B |
| AI premium at Series A | AI median **$78M** vs non-AI **$42.4M** pre-money, an 84% markup. Valuation step-up 2.2x for AI vs 1.6x for non-AI | PitchBook via the same sources | B |
| Carta software Series A (last 6 months, ~1,000 rounds) | Median raise **$14.4M**, median valuation **$80M** (the source doesn't say whether this is pre- or post-money). Record high in Q2 2026; the top 5% exceed $500M post-money | [Carta "Series A liftoff"](https://carta.com/data/newsletter-series-a-liftoff/) | B (403 to fetch; figures from the search summary) |
| Series A dilution | Median **17.9%** in Q1 2025 (20.9% a year earlier) | Carta Q1 2025, via [peony.ink](https://peony.ink/blog/startup-fundraising-benchmarks-q1-2026) | B |
| Time from seed to Series A | **616 days (~20 months)** in Q2 2025; 774 days in Q4 2024 | Carta, via [blog.mean.ceo](https://blog.mean.ceo/?p=5725) | B/C |
| ARR at Series A | Median **$2.8M** in 2025 (up from $2.3M in 2024; $1.2M in 2021). Software median is above $3M; the 75th percentile is above **$7M** | [Carta: ARR at Series A](https://carta.com/data/newsletter-arr-at-series-a/), [Carta: $7M ARR = top quartile](https://carta.com/data/linkedin-7m-arr-series-a-saas-2025/) | B (A publisher) |
| Seed round | PitchBook Q1 2026 median pre-money **$18.4M**, round **$3.0M**. Carta software seed median post-money **$21.6–24.3M** | [waveup](https://waveup.com/blog/seed-round-benchmarks/), [causo](https://hub.causo.ai/guides/seed-round-valuation-benchmark-2026) | C (citing A) |
| Europe | Atomico State of European Tech: **average** (not median) Series A **$10.6M**, up from $9.3M | [Maddyness](https://www.maddyness.com/2025/11/19/les-startups-europeennes-ont-leve-44-milliards-de-dollars-en-2025/), [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/?p=2917407) | B |
| Megadeal concentration | Rounds of $100M+ took **87.5%** of US VC dollars in H1 2026 | PitchBook via TheNextWeb | B |

**What this means for scoup.ai:** the premium valuations go to AI companies with $3M+ ARR. With no customers, scoup.ai is a seed or pre-seed company. Plan for roughly a $3M seed at about $18M pre-money (the US median), then a Series A only after reaching about $2–3M ARR, roughly 20 months later.

### 2. Burn, runway and headcount

| Metric | Value | Source | Grade |
|---|---|---|---|
| 
[...]
ftware-developers.htm))
- Computer and information research scientists (a proxy for ML engineers): **$140,300**
- Information security analysts: **$129,180**
- Sales engineers: **$124,900**
- Technical and scientific sales representatives (a proxy for an AE's base pay): **$104,920**

Startup pay for ML and SaaS AE roles runs above these medians. I couldn't retrieve Levels.fyi or AE quota/OTE data before the search limit.

**US load factor:** benefits are **30.0%** of total compensation (wages 70.0%) in BLS employer-cost data for June 2026 ([BLS ECEC](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/ecec.nr0.htm), A). That means fully loaded cost ≈ base × 1.43. For high earners the factor is lower (about 1.25–1.35, estimate C), because they pass the Social Security wage cap.

**Norway:**
- SSB average monthly pay, November 2025: **NOK 62,070** for all sectors and **NOK 80,770** for information and communication, which is about NOK 969k a year ([SSB](https://www.ssb.no/arbeid-og-lonn/lonn-og-arbeidskraftkostnader/statistikk/lonn), A).
- "Andre programvare- og applikasjonsutviklere": median **NOK 804k**, interquartile range 650k–997k (SSB via [smartepenger](https://www.smartepenger.no/jobb/2895-lonnsnivaet-i-forskjellige-yrker), C).
- Employer social security (arbeidsgiveravgift) is **14.1%** in zone I ([Skatteetaten](https://www.skatteetaten.no/satser/arbeidsgiveravgift/), A).
- Mandatory occupational pension is at least 2%. Tech firms typically pay 5–7% (C, not verified this session).
- Rough Norwegian load factor is about 1.20–1.25 (C, my calculation from the rates above).

**Compliance:**
- SOC 2 Type II auditor fee: **$20–80k**. All-in first year for a company of 25–200 people: **$50–110k** ([getagency](https://blog.getagency.com/articles/soc-2-audit-cost-for-startups), [scrut](https://www.scrut.io/post/cost-of-soc-2-audit)), C.
- Penetration test: SaaS web app plus API typically **$15–35k** at Series A–B. The overall market ranges $5–30k ([Astra](https://www.getastra.com/blog/penetration-testing/cost/), [Blaze](https://www.blazeinfosec.com/post/how-much-does-penetration-testing-cost/)), C.

**Not obtained:** AWS run-rate (the AWS pricing page tables didn't render), cyber and E&O insurance premiums, and US entity or FMC counsel hourly rates. Use the AWS Pricing Calculator against the repo's `infra/` Terraform, and get broker and counsel quotes.

### 4. B2B SaaS go-to-market benchmarks

| Metric | Value | Source | Grade |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gross margin | Median **77%** of total revenue; **81%** for subscription revenue alone | [Benchmarkit 2025](https://www.benchmarkit.ai/2025benchmarks) | B |
| Net revenue retention / gross revenue retention | Median **101% / 88%** | Benchmarkit | B |
| New CAC ratio | **$2.00** of spend per $1 of new ARR, up 14% year on year. That implies CAC payback of about 31 months at 77% gross margin (my derivation), and a magic number of about 0.5 | Benchmarkit | B |
| Series A readiness | NRR above 110%, CAC payback under 12 months, gross margin above 70% | [waveup](https://waveup.com/blog/series-a-benchmarks/) | C |
| Growth | Private B2B SaaS median **22%** (2026 survey); Benchmarkit median 26% | [SaaS Capital](https://www.saas-capital.com/research/private-saas-company-growth-rate-benchmarks/) | B |
| Contingency fees for freight recovery | **Refund Retriever: 50%** of recoveries up to $250k annual shipping spend, **45%** up to $500k, **40%** up to $1M, custom above that. **LateShipment OneAudit: 35%** | [Refund Retriever pricing](https://www.refundretriever.com/pricing), [LateShipment pricing](https://www.lateshipment.com/pricing) | A (official price pages; these are parcel audit firms) |
| Freight audit per invoice | Internal processing about **$11/invoice**; outsourced about 5–10% of that (~$0.55–1.10); invoice discrepancies "up to 8.8%" | [Wikipedia: Freight audit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freight_audit) | C (citations weak) |

Sales cycle length for mid-market logistics software: **not found**.

### 5. Logistics-tech VC context

- Supply chain and logistics startups raised **$6.2B across ~350 deals in H1 2026**, the strongest half since 2022 (Crunchbase, B).
- **Freehand (formerly Pando)**: **$75M Series B** in July 2026, led by Battery Ventures and NewRoad Capital Partners; $100M raised in total; Series A was $25M in March 2024. It runs AI invoice verification and spend recovery on supply-chain spend and claims "5–10% of spend recovered". This is a **direct comparable or competitor** ([Crunchbase News](https://news.crunchbase.com/transportation/freehand-pando-enterprise-supply-chain-spend-management-startup/), B).
- **ClearJet**: $25M Series B in August 2026 for AI air-cargo capacity ([Crunchbase](https://news.crunchbase.com/transportation/clearjet-raises-25m-logistics-ai-seriesb/), B).
- Not retrieved: logistics-tech totals for full-year 2024 and 2025, and PitchBook's supply chain tech report (403).

### 6. The 12 numbers that matter most for sizing and the model

1. Series A requires about **$2.8M median ARR** (75th percentile above $7M). This is the gate scoup.ai must reach.
2. Software Series A raise: **$14.4M median** (Carta).
3. Series A pre-money: **$62–64M** overall, **$42.4M non-AI vs $78M AI** (PitchBook Q2 2026).
4. Series A dilution: about **18%**.
5. Seed: about **$3.0M round at $18.4M pre-money**.
6. Seed to Series A takes about **20 months** (616 days).
7. Team at Series A: about **14 FTE**.
8. Runway target: **24–30 months** (convention, C).
9. Fully loaded cost: **US base × ~1.3–1.43; Norway base × ~1.20–1.25** (14.1% employer tax plus pension).
10. Engineer base pay: **US $136k** (BLS median); **Norway about NOK 804k–969k**.
11. Unit economics: gross margin **77%**, NRR **101%**, new CAC ratio **$2.00** (median). The contingency model's services labour will push gross margin below that median.
12. Contingency take rate: **35–50% of recoveries** (posted parcel-audit prices). Model base, low and high cases at 35%, 40% and 50%.

**First-year compliance budget:** about $70–150k combined (SOC 2 all-in $50–110k plus a pentest $15–35k).

### Caveats
- Carta pages return 403 to the fetch tool, so Carta figures come from search summaries and secondary blogs. Check them against the Carta originals before putting them in investor material.
- Carta's $80M Series A figure isn't labelled pre- or post-money.
- Open gaps: AE quota and OTE, ML engineer total compensation, AWS cost, cyber and E&O premiums, FMC counsel rates, mid-market logistics sales cycle, logistics VC totals for 2024–2025, Dealroom Nordic data.
- Under the project's honesty rule, every grade-C number should be labelled as an estimate in the plan.
